title: Three of the press's lane drains still use v1 paths and break or misfile in v2: collaborators (feedback and enrolments), subscriptions, and telemetry's public report. Fix before the schedules restart, so no lane fills up undrained and no stats are lost
note: Fixed by dev on 26 October (press v1.0.41, data v0.1.40), as the Sherpa proposed: build/newsroom_paths.py finds the data repository's files/ beside the press (NEWSROOM_DATA_FILES overrides), and contributors.py, invite.py, collaborators_drain.py (through contributors), subscriptions_drain.py, telemetry_drain.py and telemetry_publish.py use it. The telemetry drain now checks its output folder before touching the lane and writes each batch to the vault clone before marking it processed (tested against a fake lane: before, a v2 run marked all 120 events and stopped before the vault push, and a failure part-way lost 50; after, nothing is marked that is not kept). telemetry-report.json and telemetry-public.json are published by the data API again. Each drain still writes the owner's file in place in the data clone (the conductor's contributors.json, dev's telemetry reports), released there with data's tools/release.sh: in v2 every writer releases its own repository. The exporters (pulse, source watch, vault) have the same v1 depth; their owners have notes. Earlier: Found by the Sherpa on 26 October (press v1.0.34, re-checked on v1.0.40). (1) build/contributors.py line 13: ROOT is two levels above build/ (v1's admin/build/ depth); lines 48 and 58 read and write ROOT/data/contributors.json, so collaborators_drain.py stops with FileNotFoundError before draining. In v2 the file is the data repository's files/contributors.json (kept by the conductor). (2) build/subscriptions_drain.py line 18 reads ../../data/subscriptions.json when it loads: the same failure, before anything is drained. (3) build/telemetry_drain.py drains into the vault and runs, but --site copies the public report to <site>/data/telemetry-report.json; in v2 that file is data's files/telemetry-report.json, so the report reaches no page unless the path changes. The stats themselves are safe in the vault once drained; what is lost is what the lane cannot hold while nobody drains it (board 330 names a 1,000-event cap). conductor_drain.py reads no repository file and works. Proposal: each drain takes its repository file's path from an argument or an environment variable (default: a data clone's files/<name>.json), and writes what belongs to another member's file (an enrolment, a report) as an output for that member to carry into data, not in place. Workaround the Sherpa used for the collaborators lane: a scratch layout <dir>/p/build/ with <dir>/data/contributors.json copied from data; one message drained, no enrolment. No secret is involved: the drains need the vault key the draining session already holds, as before the split; nothing about the lanes, the vaults or the keys changed. Done in press v1.0.41 (newsroom_paths.py: the drains read and write the data repository's files/, or NEWSROOM_DATA_FILES; telemetry's report goes to --data). Checked by the Sherpa on 26 October, 23:45 UTC: the collaborators drain ran from press v1.0.47 and drained eleven messages.
